## Overview

This dossier draws on the **[Economic Forecast](../document-types/economic-forecast.qmd)** published by the **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)** on 2026-05-21. The main themes include a recovery in real GDP growth driven by domestic demand, a widening general government deficit due to discretionary tax cuts and defense spending, and a modest increase in the gross debt-to-GDP ratio.

#### Other growth context

- **C1\*, context**: Real GDP growth is projected at 1.8% in 2026 and 2.2% in 2027. The recovery is driven by domestic demand, though temporarily slowed by geopolitical developments. Household consumption growth is set to average just above 2% in both years. Private investment growth is supported by a recovery in residential construction, while public investment, particularly on defense, is the most dynamic component. Net exports are expected to have a slightly negative contribution to growth in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 162" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 162">ⓘ</button>

#### Other inflation context

- **Context**: The Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) year-on-year growth is projected at 2.6% in 2025, declining to 1.5% in 2026, and rising slightly to 1.8% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 163" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 163">ⓘ</button>

#### Other fiscal context

- **C3\*, context**: The general government deficit is projected to increase to 2.8% of GDP in 2026, due to discretionary fiscal measures adding up to around 2% of GDP, including tax reductions (income tax and temporary VAT reduction on food) and increased spending on defense and support to Ukraine. The fiscal stance shifts to expansive in 2026 (1.9% of GDP) but returns to slightly contractive in 2027 (0.3%). The deficit is set to decrease to 2.5% of GDP in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 163" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 163">ⓘ</button>

## Outlook Material

- **Context**: Geopolitical developments have temporarily slowed domestic demand-driven recovery. Increased defense spending and support to Ukraine are contributing to higher public expenditure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 162-163" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 162-163">ⓘ</button>
